titulo: The future: werden and Futur I: Werden as a verb

aula.titulo: The future: werden and Futur I
aula.objetivo: Conjugate «werden», use it as a main verb ("to become") and as the future auxiliary (werden + infinitive), and know when the present tense with a time word is enough to talk about the future.

blocos.texto: Lesson goal. By the end of the four sessions, you talk about the future with the present tense + a time word, use werden + infinitive to promise, predict and assume, use werden in the sense of "to become", and ask «Was hast du vor?» (What are you planning?).

blocos.contexto: Jonas asks Camila what she's going to do on vacation.

linhas.ru: — Camila, was machst du im Sommer?
linhas.pt: — Camila, what are you going to do this summer?
linhas.audio: Camila, was machst du im Sommer?

linhas.ru: — Ich fliege nach Brasilien. Ich besuche meine Familie in Recife.
linhas.pt: — I'm flying to Brazil. I'm going to visit my family in Recife.
linhas.audio: Ich fliege nach Brasilien. Ich besuche meine Familie in Recife.

linhas.pt: — How long are you going to stay?

linhas.ru: — Vier Wochen. Ich werde meine Oma besuchen und viel schlafen. Pedro holt mich am Flughafen ab.
linhas.pt: — Four weeks. I'm going to visit my grandma and sleep a lot. Pedro is picking me up at the airport.
linhas.audio: Vier Wochen. Ich werde meine Oma besuchen und viel schlafen. Pedro holt mich am Flughafen ab.

linhas.ru: — Wow! Und was wirst du in Recife essen?
linhas.pt: — Wow! And what are you going to eat in Recife?
linhas.audio: Wow! Und was wirst du in Recife essen?

linhas.ru: — Tapioca, natürlich! Und du? Was hast du vor?
linhas.pt: — Tapioca, of course! And you? What are you planning?
linhas.audio: Tapioca, natürlich! Und du? Was hast du vor?

linhas.ru: — Ich werde in München bleiben und arbeiten. Aber im Herbst fahre ich nach Wien.
linhas.pt: — I'm staying in Munich and working. But in the fall I'm going to Vienna.
linhas.audio: Ich werde in München bleiben und arbeiten. Aber im Herbst fahre ich nach Wien.

blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: everyday German future = present tense + a time word: «Morgen fahre ich nach Berlin» (I'm going to Berlin tomorrow). STEP 2: werden + infinitive at the end is for promises, predictions and assumptions. STEP 3: "going to" is NOT «gehen» + infinitive. STEP 4: the big false friend: «Ich will» means "I want", not "I will". "I will" is «Ich werde».

tabela.ingles: He's going to be a doctor (becomes a doctor).

blocos.titulo: Werden: "become" and the future, step by step
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: «werden» is irregular: ich werde, du wirst, er wird, wir werden, ihr werdet, sie werden. STEP 2: as a MAIN VERB, «werden» means TO BECOME, TO GET: «Es wird kalt» (it's getting cold), «Ich werde Lehrer» (I'm going to be a teacher — literally "I become a teacher"), «Er wird müde» (he's getting tired). STEP 3: as the future AUXILIARY, «werden» + infinitive at the END forms the FUTUR I: «Ich werde morgen arbeiten» (I will work tomorrow). STEP 4: the verb bracket again: «werden» in 2nd position and the infinitive at the end. STEP 5: question: «Wirst du kommen?» (Will you come?); negative: «Ich werde nicht kommen» (I won't come). STEP 6: with a separable verb, the whole infinitive goes to the end: «Ich werde früh aufstehen.»
blocos.comparacao: English "will" + verb is the closest match ("I will work" = «Ich werde arbeiten»), but German uses it far less: most of the time, the present tense with «morgen», «nächste Woche» or «bald» does the job. And never confuse «werden» (will, become) with «wollen» (want): «Ich will kommen» = I want to come.

tabela.exemplo: Es wird kalt. / Er wird kommen.

erros.motivo: The infinitive goes to the end.

blocos.enunciado: Say 6 sentences with «werden»: «Es wird kalt. Ich werde Lehrer. Ich werde morgen … arbeiten.»
Write 8 polite requests and pieces of advice with würde, hätte, wäre and könnte.
